subject.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata

question: Should structured `exec.approval.requested` events become the source of truth for ACP permission `title` and `toolCallId`, or should ACP keep fallback metadata for early structured events and rely on later agent approval events?
rationale: The proposed parser-only fix assumes a Gateway payload contract that current schema, types, and producers do not provide; choosing where approval metadata should originate affects a user-facing permission boundary.

options.title: Add contract-backed exec metadata
options.body: Extend the exec approval request schema/types/producers to carry sanitized `title` and `toolCallId`, then keep the ACP parser mapping and add a translator-level regression from an actual structured event.

options.title: Keep structured fallback
options.body: Reject the parser-only metadata mapping and keep early structured exec approval events using `exec:<approvalId>` until a broader approval event redesign is sponsored.

options.title: Defer to a protocol follow-up
options.body: Close or pause this PR and open a narrower owner-backed design item for approval metadata propagation across Gateway and ACP.

recommendation.title: Add contract-backed exec metadata
recommendation.body: Extend the exec approval request schema/types/producers to carry sanitized `title` and `toolCallId`, then keep the ACP parser mapping and add a translator-level regression from an actual structured event.

likelyOwner.reason: amknight authored and merged the ACP exec approval relay that defines the current early structured-event fallback behavior.
